doc.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: The missing foot pedal on a Tiny Bradshaw job
summary: Joe Medlin and Major Holley called him at short notice to play with Tiny Bradshaw in Jersey; he forgot the foot pedal and Art Blakey sent one.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: What kind of dances were they doing at this point? What year was it?

Fifties. Late fifties. Medium fifties, you know. Yeah, medium fifties, late fifties around that time, going into the sixties. Well they were doing the Lindy, formal, like ballroom, they were doing mambos. The mambo was coming out. Then a lot of Latin and mambo and stuff like that. And calypso, they did calypso, jitterbug, swing-type dancing, ballroom dancing, and they always did some kind of creative things, you know. So I used to get a lot of gigs playing with some groups, local groups and I remember one time, this is a funny story I have to tell this one. I had a new set of drums set up in my grandmother’s © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

living room and I was staying with her at the time. And somebody had given my number, I don’t know if it was Major Holley or Joe Medlin, whoever, but I got a call, they said, “Jackie, are you playing tonight?” I said, “No.” They said, “Well we got a job, we have to have —” “Well,” I said, “I don’t know, I’d been trying, I had just took them out of the boxes, they’re all—” They say, “Well we’re in a hurry, we got to have you right away, we’re coming to get you.” I said, “Well wait a minute.” They said, “No we can’t wait. You’re not working so we’re coming.” And I said, “Well wait —” And I said, “Okay, come on. But I got to put all this stuff together, it’s all scattered all over.” They said, “Don’t worry about it we’ll take care of it.” So they got there, it was Joe Medlin the singer, and Major Holley came. They’re playing for Tiny Bradshaw. They said, “Hurry up. Let’s get this stuff here.” I said, “Well gee whiz, you know, I’m not dressed.” They said, “Well go on and get dressed, we’re going to put this set together.” So I say oh Lord, why did I get into this? So finally we got it all together — they got it together. So we’re on the way out to Jersey to this I think we was playing at the Mosque or one of those places out there. And you know, we were in the tunnel, the Holland Tunnel coming across. And I said, “You know, something is wrong here. I don’t remember putting something — packing something — I think the foot pedal.” They said, “Don’t worry about it, you’ve probably got it.” And I’m thinking to myself, you know how you get that feeling, and all that rush and hurry you know. So we got there, and I’m setting up all these drums and everything. And there’s no foot pedal. And I said, “I knew it, I knew it.” So, and I asked Tiny Bradshaw, who was a stomping band, you know, he wanted to hear it you know? You know Tiny and those guys, they were known for that strong beat.

And especially the foot. So I’m playing and you know Major’s looking at me. And so finally, Joe said, all right Jackie. Art Blakey was working not too far from there. Thank God he was working close by. So they went up and told Art Blakey, and Art sent me a foot pedal. So I finished the gig out. But it was so funny at one point because after that happened, Major says, “You mean to tell me you worked me to death?” You know how funny he is. And he would stop people, and he would put yeast in the story. And I’d say now Major, don’t lie, it was just the foot pedal that I left. He tells people, “You know what he did? He came on this gig with a brand new set of drums — no sticks, no brushes, no nothing. And he worked me to death.” So I said, “Why Major, I know that you’re such a great bass player, I figured you didn’t even need it.” And he’d say, “Why you!” He was so beautiful. We had so much fun together you know. We worked together quite a bit even since and after that you know. He was just such a great player. I sure miss him too. He was a wonderful player. But that was such a hilarious experience.
